Reach code flower client on this computer from any browser or phone, through a code flower tunnel (https://tunnels.codeflower.app, or your own: "tunnel: &#123;url: …&#125;" in config.yaml).

```sh
codeflower tunnel pair     pair a browser: open the link it prints there
```

Pairing signs this computer in when needed ("codeflower tunnel login") and starts code flower client in the background, which keeps the tunnel connected and lists every sandbox on this computer: those it starts, and those "codeflower run" and "codeflower sandbox" start in a terminal (they start the client themselves while this computer is signed in and remote access is on).

Everything between a paired browser and this computer is end-to-end encrypted; the tunnel cannot read it. Signing in to the tunnel alone does not give access: a browser must also be paired here.

A paired browser can use your sandboxes' chats, which run code in the sandboxes. "tunnel: &#123;hardened: true&#125;" limits each browser to the sandboxes chosen when pairing it and confines the connector (Linux). "tunnel: &#123;manage: true&#125;" also lets paired browsers start sandboxes and browse folders.


## Usage

```sh
codeflower tunnel
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config string` |  | config directory with config.yaml (or set $CODEFLOWER_CONFIG; default ~/.codeflower) |

## Commands

- [`codeflower tunnel devices`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-devices/): List the paired browsers
- [`codeflower tunnel login`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-login/): Sign this computer in to the tunnel
- [`codeflower tunnel logout`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-logout/): Sign this computer out of the tunnel and forget its key and paired browsers
- [`codeflower tunnel off`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-off/): Turn remote access off at once (pairings are kept)
- [`codeflower tunnel on`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-on/): Turn remote access on again
- [`codeflower tunnel pair`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-pair/): Pair a browser: prints a link (and a QR code) to open there
- [`codeflower tunnel revoke`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-revoke/): Unpair a browser, by its name or fingerprint (as "devices" lists them); its open chats close at once
- [`codeflower tunnel rotate`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-rotate/): Give this computer a new key; every browser must pair again
- [`codeflower tunnel status`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-status/): Show the tunnel connection, this computer's key and the tunnel's compatibility
- [`codeflower tunnel verify`](/reference/cli/codeflower-tunnel-verify/): Check that the tunnel serves the browser code this code flower expects
